scope: Corollary 10.1 of the manuscript “A Fully Polynomial Randomized Approximation Scheme for Perfect Matchings in General Graphs” (preprints/A-Fully-Polynomial-Randomized-Approximation-Scheme-for-Perfect-Matchings-in-General-Graphs-September-23-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 113 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 1510b15725ee7e92), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 41. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For either family A = F(G, f) or A = Mk(G), there are uniform classical randomized algorithms with the following guarantees. (i) Given rational 0 < ε < 1 and 0 < δ < 1/2, the counting algorithm returns a nonnegative rational ̂ N such that P[(1 − ε)|A| ≤ ̂ N ≤ (1 + ε)|A|] ≥ 1 − δ. If A is empty, it returns zero with certainty. Its bit running time on every execution is polynomial in the full input encoding length, ε−1, and log δ−1. (ii) Given rational 0 < τ < 1, the sampling algorithm reports infeasibility exactly when A is empty. Otherwise it returns a member X of A on every execution, and TV(L(X), UA) ≤ τ, where UA is the uniform law on A and TV(µ, ν) = 1 2 ∑ x |µ(x) − ν(x)|. Its bit running time on every execution is polynomial in the full input encoding length and τ−1.
